feedback.goal: Correct the unsupported HMR readiness and imported-closure assumptions, then quarantine candidate application without removing inactive staging.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Candidate application fails before approval verification or any live-file write.
Candidate rejection never overwrites live files that changed after staging.
No coordinator or production recorder path can create or trust an admitted HMR candidate generation.
Opt-in executable evidence reproduces pre-readiness reload observation, failed startup without baseline restoration, and hybrid multi-file activation.
Canonical documentation and capsules own the quarantine decision, and the complete repository gate passes.

outcome.summary: HMR candidate application and in-process admission are code-quarantined; inactive staging remains, current DSH risks are executable evidence, and all final verification gates pass.

what_worked: Exact source inspection separated HMR event delivery from replacement-Fiber readiness.
Real DSH probes made failed-start and multi-file imported-closure gaps falsifiable.
Removing publication and approval execution was smaller and safer than preserving an unusable admission state machine.
Repeated focused review found and closed erased-private, mutable-service, and prototype-shadowing bypasses before publication.
what_failed: The superseded design treated hmr/reload and event-time disk digests as admission evidence without testing readiness or imported closure identity.
The first full repository gate used a stale capsule validation date; after correction, one retry encountered transient shared-store test interference before the final gate passed.

failures_and_inefficiencies.summary: Initial quarantine retained runtime-callable TypeScript-private mutation and mutable generation seams that required additional hardening rounds.
failures_and_inefficiencies.suggested_action: Threat-review emitted JavaScript visibility and same-realm service mutation whenever a TypeScript private member protects an authority boundary.

failures_and_inefficiencies.summary: The repository gate required retries for a pinned capsule date and one non-reproducing shared-store test race.
failures_and_inefficiencies.suggested_action: Keep capsule validation dates synchronized and isolate repository-level test stores when that separate test-maintenance work is scheduled.

evidence.summary: ADR 0007 supersedes HMR admission and defines the readiness, imported-closure, rollback, and recovery prerequisites for reconsideration.
The coordinator writes only fixed staging targets, fails application immediately, refuses drifted rejection, and protects non-admitted state from same-runtime method replacement.
The production recorder no longer trusts mutable in-process candidate service state for evaluation eligibility.
Three focused suites passed 27 tests with 6 opt-in skips after final hardening.
All 6 coordinator tests passed, including executable failed-start and hybrid-closure probes against pinned DSH evidence.
All three capsules validated with quarantine-aware claims and current source digests.
The final gate passed typecheck, build, 34 test files with 214 passing tests and 7 opt-in skips, capsule validation, policy checks, core evaluation, and benchmark evaluation without a hard stop.
Final focused review reported no findings; residual risk is limited to the explicitly unsupported DSH HMR readiness and same-realm containment boundaries.

uncertainty.statement: Current DSH HMR still lacks authoritative imported-closure identity, awaited replacement readiness, and failed-start rollback.
uncertainty.resolution: Keep admission quarantined while private evaluator Phase 3 gathers version-pinned lifecycle evidence and an upstream contract is designed.

uncertainty.statement: Non-overridable coordinator methods prevent accidental authority spoofing but do not make arbitrary same-realm code a security sandbox.
uncertainty.resolution: Keep trusted evaluation and any future deployment authority outside the candidate process.
